::: {.bottom-line}
**Bottom line.** Bender's most-used word is his own name (206 times), then "fry" (158). "Ass" is only his 7th most-used word, but he says it 67 times, more than anyone else in the show.
:::

In "War Is the H-Word," the plot turns on a bomb that will go off when Bender says his most-used word. Fans have always assumed they know what that word is. I counted every word Bender says across all 140 episodes to check.

<!-- TODO (Sean): confirm the premise wording against the episode. -->

## His top word is his own name

Bender talks about Bender a lot. After removing common words like "the" and "I," and filler like "hey" and "yeah," his own name tops the list, followed by his best friend's.


::: {.cell renderings='["light","dark"]'}

```{.r .cell-code}
plot_top <- function(mode) {
  top_words |>
    filter(rank <= 15) |>
    slice_head(n = 15) |>
    mutate(word = fct_reorder(word, n), is_ass = word == "ass") |>
    ggplot(aes(n, word, fill = is_ass)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.72) +
    geom_text(aes(label = n, fontface = ifelse(is_ass, "bold", "plain")),
              hjust = -0.25, size = 3.6, colour = label_ink(mode)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = pe_green, `TRUE` = focus)) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
    labs(x = "Times said", y = NULL) +
    theme_pe(mode)
}
plot_top("light")
plot_top("dark")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Bender's 15 most-used words](index_files/figure-html/top-words-1.png){fig-alt='Horizontal bar chart of Bender\'s 15 most-used words. \'bender\' leads, followed by \'fry\' and \'robot\'; \'ass\' is highlighted in seventh place.' width=672}
:::

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Bender's 15 most-used words](index_files/figure-html/top-words-2.png){fig-alt='Horizontal bar chart of Bender\'s 15 most-used words. \'bender\' leads, followed by \'fry\' and \'robot\'; \'ass\' is highlighted in seventh place.' width=672}
:::
:::


Ties share a rank, so "god" and "guys" are both 9th. Stemming, which folds "asses" into "ass" but also merges other words' variants, drops "ass" to 10th.

## Nobody says "ass" more

He may not say it most often, but he says it more than anyone else, and it isn't close. Fry is a distant second with 14.


::: {.cell renderings='["light","dark"]'}

```{.r .cell-code}
plot_ass <- function(mode) {
  ass_users |>
    slice_max(ass_exact, n = 8, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    mutate(speaker = fct_reorder(speaker, ass_exact), is_bender = speaker == "Bender") |>
    ggplot(aes(ass_exact, speaker, fill = is_bender)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.72) +
    geom_text(aes(label = ass_exact), hjust = -0.3, size = 3.6, colour = label_ink(mode)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = pe_green, `TRUE` = focus)) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
    labs(x = "Times said \"ass\"", y = NULL) +
    theme_pe(mode)
}
plot_ass("light")
plot_ass("dark")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Who says "ass" most](index_files/figure-html/ass-users-1.png){fig-alt='Horizontal bar chart of the characters who say \'ass\' most. Bender is far ahead of everyone else; Fry and Leela follow with under 20 each.' width=672}
:::

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Who says "ass" most](index_files/figure-html/ass-users-2.png){fig-alt='Horizontal bar chart of the characters who say \'ass\' most. Bender is far ahead of everyone else; Fry and Leela follow with under 20 each.' width=672}
:::
:::




## Per word spoken, it's closer

Bender also talks more than almost anyone, so raw counts flatter him. Scaling by how much each character says changes the picture: among characters with at least 2,000 words, Mom says "ass" at a slightly higher rate. That rests on just 5 uses, though, so I wouldn't put much weight on it.


::: {.cell renderings='["light","dark"]'}

```{.r .cell-code}
rate_data <- totals |>
  filter(words >= 2000) |>
  left_join(select(ass_users, speaker, ass_exact), by = "speaker") |>
  filter(coalesce(ass_exact, 0) > 0) |>   # characters who say it at least once
  mutate(
         rate = 1e4 * ass_exact / words,
         speaker = fct_reorder(speaker, rate),
         is_bender = speaker == "Bender")

plot_rate <- function(mode) {
  ggplot(rate_data, aes(rate, speaker, colour = is_bender)) +
    geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = rate, yend = speaker), linewidth = 0.6, alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_point(size = 3.2) +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(ass_exact, ifelse(ass_exact == 1, " use", " uses"))), hjust = -0.25, size = 3.3,
              colour = if (mode == "light") "#5f6670" else "#aab1ba") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = pe_green, `TRUE` = focus)) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25))) +
    labs(x = "Per 10,000 words spoken", y = NULL) +
    theme_pe(mode)
}
plot_rate("light")
plot_rate("dark")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
!["Ass" per 10,000 words spoken (characters with 2,000+ words who say it at least once)](index_files/figure-html/ass-rate-1.png){fig-alt='Dot chart of \'ass\' per 10,000 words for main characters. Mom and Bender lead at around 16 to 20 per 10,000 words; everyone else is under 7.' width=672}
:::

::: {.cell-output-display}
!["Ass" per 10,000 words spoken (characters with 2,000+ words who say it at least once)](index_files/figure-html/ass-rate-2.png){fig-alt='Dot chart of \'ass\' per 10,000 words for main characters. Mom and Bender lead at around 16 to 20 per 10,000 words; everyone else is under 7.' width=672}
:::
:::


## The episode's list vs. the real counts

<!-- TODO (Sean): confirm these are the words shown in the episode. -->

Here are the words on the episode's list, with how often Bender actually says each. Several barely register, and three are common words ("my," "up," "yours") that word counts usually leave out.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
claimed |>
  arrange(desc(n), word) |>
  transmute(
    Word = word,
    `Times Bender says it` = n,
    `Rank among all his words` = ifelse(is.na(rank_all_words), "never said", scales::ordinal(rank_all_words, big.mark = ",")),
    `Rank after removing common words` = case_when(
      is_stop_word ~ "removed (common word)",
      is.na(rank_content_words) ~ "never said",
      TRUE ~ scales::ordinal(rank_content_words, big.mark = ",")
    )
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrr")
```

## Explore any character's words

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
words = FileAttachment("data/character_word_counts.csv").csv({typed: true})
speakers = Array.from(new Set(words.map(d => d.speaker))).sort()
viewof who = Inputs.select(speakers, {label: "Character", value: "Bender"})
topN = words.filter(d => d.speaker === who).sort((a, b) => b.n - a.n).slice(0, 15)

Plot.plot({
  marginLeft: 90,
  marginRight: 40,
  height: 420,
  x: {label: "Times said", grid: true},
  y: {label: null},
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(topN, {
      x: "n", y: "word", sort: {y: "-x"},
      fill: d => d.word === "ass" ? "#D9762B" : "#2E9E68",
      tip: {format: {fill: false}},
      title: d => `${d.word}: ${d.n} times (${d.per_1k_words.toFixed(1)} per 1,000 words)`
    }),
    Plot.text(topN, {x: "n", y: "word", text: d => d.n, dx: 4, textAnchor: "start", fill: "currentColor"}),
    Plot.ruleX([0])
  ]
})
```

Covers the 12 characters with at least 2,000 words of dialogue; common words and filler are removed.

## How this was done

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Methods and limitations

**Data.** Transcripts of all 140 broadcast episodes from [The Infosphere](https://theinfosphere.org), collected in 2023. The 140 include the four films, which aired as 16 "Part" episodes. Only aggregated counts are published here; the transcripts and scraping code are not.

**Cleaning.** Most transcript pages had never been split into speaker and line, so I re-split every line on its first colon. That kept 1,010 lines that contain a second colon, which my 2023 version cut off. Stage directions in brackets and parentheses are removed from both the speaker and the line. Alternate-universe, robot, and ghost versions of the main cast count as the same character. The result is 28,949 spoken lines.

**Words.** Tokenized with tidytext. Common words are removed using tidytext's stop-word lists, plus interjections and filler ("hey," "yeah," "uh," "gonna," and stretched spellings like "ohhhh"). Stemming uses the Porter stemmer. Ties share a rank.

**Why remove filler.** With stop words alone, "hey" edges out "bender" as his top word:


::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}


|Definition                                |Top five                                                    |
|:-----------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------|
|Stop words and filler removed (used here) |bender (206), fry (158), robot (123), time (84), wait (83)  |
|Stop words only                           |hey (212), bender (206), yeah (172), fry (158), robot (123) |


:::
:::


**What changed from 2023.** The original version of this analysis (published on LinkedIn) counted "bender" 375 times. That was inflated: its cleaning removed parenthetical directions but left bracketed ones like "[Bender walks in]" in the dialogue.

**Limitations.** Two episodes are mostly missing from the source: "Naturama" is one unsplit block of text and "Saturday Morning Fun Pit" largely is too, so those blocks are left out. "Zapp Dingbat" and "Meanwhile" have short transcripts at the source. Fan transcripts also miss or mishear some lines.
:::
